EVENT 4 · TRAINING CAVE

Grammar: always or now?

First the time word. It tells you which verb to use.

Why are there two present tenses? English always asks: is it always true, or is it happening now?

Lions eat meat. (always: every day, all their life) · Look! The lion is eating. (now: at this moment)

ALWAYS · present simple

Facts and habits.

Time words: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day, at night, on Saturdays

  • Lions eat meat.
  • A dolphin swims very fast.
  • What do lions eat? They eat meat.
  • Does a shark sleep? Yes, it does.

I / you / we / they eat · he / she / it eats

NOW · present continuous

It is happening at this moment.

Time words: now, right now, at the moment, Look!, Listen!, Shh!

  • Look! The lion is sleeping now.
  • The monkeys are climbing at the moment.
  • What is the lion doing now? It's sleeping.
  • Is the monkey climbing? Yes, it is.

am / is / are + verb-ing

Step 1: find the time word

every day, usually → always

now, Look! → now

Step 2: always → he / she / it + s

A seal swims. A lion hunts.

Questions: Do lions …? Does a lion …?

Step 3: now → am / is / are + -ing

The seal is swimming.

swim → swimming · hide → hiding · Is it …ing?

always, usually, often, sometimes, never

Before the main verb: Lions usually sleep in the day.

After am / is / are: The lion is often hungry.

Don't say The lion sleeping now. → The lion is sleeping now. Lions are eat meat. → Lions eat meat. Does the monkey climbing? → Is the monkey climbing? A shark swim fast. → A shark swims fast.

BONUS EVENT · REPLAY

Reading: Rosie's zoo day

Read Rosie's blog. Then answer the questions.

Rosie's Blog

Saturday, 11 am

by Rosie Wilson

Hi from the zoo! I'm here with Dan and Nora today. It's sunny, and there are lots of people here. Right now Nora is watching the seals. A zoo keeper is feeding them, and they are playing with a ball.

Dan isn't looking at the animals. He's taking photos for his blog. I'm sitting next to the hippos. Hippos usually stay in the water in the day, and they eat grass at night. Look! One hippo is opening its big mouth.

Every Saturday I swim at the pool, but today I'm at the zoo. What a great day!
